entries.core_move: Transform an LTI convolution output $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$ with the one-sided Laplace transform to replace time-domain convolution by multiplication of $X(s)$ and $H(s)$ in transfer-function analysis.
Translate the LTI input-output convolution relation $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$ into $Y(s)=X(s)H(s)$ and identify $X(s)$, $H(s)$, and $Y(s)$ as the input, system, and output transforms.
Isolate $H(s)$ from the Laplace-domain input-output relation by dividing $Y(s)$ by $X(s)$ and interpret the result as the system-only multiplier for an LTI system.
Relate an LTI system's impulse response $h(t)$ to its transfer function $H(s)$ by using the Laplace transform to connect the time-domain convolution kernel with the $s$-domain multiplier.
Recognize a transfer function as rational by expressing $H(s)$ as a quotient of polynomials in $s$, the form used for later pole, zero, and stability analysis.
Separate a rational transfer function $H(s)$ into numerator and denominator polynomials and connect numerator roots to zeros and denominator roots to poles for later $s$-plane and stability analysis.
